alerts.title: Low phosphate with TDF — possible tubulopathy
alerts.message: TDF can cause renal tubular wasting syndrome, including phosphate wasting. Patient on TDF for 6 years with serum phosphate 0.78 mmol/L and trace proteinuria. Creatinine 112 umol/L is within normal limits but does not exclude early tubular dysfunction. Evidence for drug attribution: TDF is a known cause of tubular wasting, and hypophosphataemia plus proteinuria are characteristic. Evidence against: occupational factors and poor BP control could contribute to proteinuria; phosphate level is only mildly reduced. Guidelines recommend eGFR monitoring at 6–12 monthly intervals on TDF, and more frequent monitoring in high-risk patients including those with co-existent hypertension.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate eGFR; trend phosphate and proteinuria; consider TDF substitution with TAF if tubular dysfunction confirmed. Monitor renal function more frequently given hypertension.

alerts.title: TDF plus ibuprofen — compounding renal risk
alerts.message: TDF is nephrotoxic and guidelines caution about renal deterioration during intercurrent illness or with other renal stressors. Patient routinely takes over-the-counter ibuprofen for chronic back pain while on TDF. NSAIDs reduce renal perfusion and can precipitate acute kidney injury, particularly in patients on nephrotoxic ART. This patient also has hypertension and trace proteinuria, further elevating renal risk. The clinician's plan refills ibuprofen PRN without flagging the TDF–NSAID interaction or recommending renal monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel on minimizing ibuprofen use; consider non-NSAID analgesia for chronic back pain. Check eGFR before continued NSAID use and monitor renal function if ibuprofen cannot be avoided.

alerts.title: eGFR not calculated despite TDF and hypertension
alerts.message: Guidelines require eGFR monitoring at 3 months, 6 months, then 6–12 monthly on TDF, and specify more frequent monitoring in high-risk patients with co-existent hypertension. Patient has hypertension (BP 146/94) and trace proteinuria but only a serum creatinine was recorded; no eGFR was calculated or documented. Additionally, no baseline or follow-up phosphate was planned despite the abnormal result. The 6-month review interval without renal surveillance is suboptimal given the patient's risk profile.

evidence.recommended_action: Calculate and document eGFR today; schedule repeat eGFR, phosphate, and urinalysis within 3 months. Shorten follow-up interval to allow renal monitoring.

alerts.title: Uncontrolled hypertension increases TDF renal risk
alerts.message: Guidelines identify co-existent hypertension as a high-risk factor requiring intensified TDF renal monitoring. Patient's BP is 146/94 with admitted amlodipine non-adherence, and trace proteinuria is present. The plan simply refills amlodipine without intensifying antihypertensive management or addressing the interaction between uncontrolled hypertension and TDF nephrotoxicity. Persistent hypertension with proteinuria on TDF raises concern for compounded renal injury over time.

evidence.recommended_action: Address amlodipine adherence; consider dose increase or addition of a second antihypertensive. Recheck BP within 4 weeks and intensify renal monitoring while BP remains uncontrolled.
